newsitem.title: UK: Open skies hinges on BA/AA go-ahead-Delta.
newsitem.headline: Open skies hinges on BA/AA go-ahead-Delta.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc., one of the biggest U.S. airlines, said on Monday it believed an "open skies" deal would not be fully ratified until the transatlantic alliance betweeen British Airways and American Airlines is cleared.

Scott Yohe, senior vice-president of government affairs at Delta, told Reuters in a telephone interview that he believed full agreement was not possible between the UK and U.S. this time round but was likely in subsequent talks. But Yohe added that he expected any open skies pact to be initialled first and only fully ratified once the BA/AA deal is sealed.
Yohe said a similar process had been used in the open skies talks between Germany and the U.S.
"Germany wanted to link clearance of the alliance between Lufthansa and United Airlines and open skies," said Yohe, leading to the pact being initialled until the alliance was cleared in the U.S.
Another possible sticking point to talks is the UK's move to secure some protection for smaller transatlantic carriers who may suffer once all-out competition is implemented under liberalisation.
But Delta said it believed the U.S. government was highly unlikely to agree to this change as it would be a departure from the standard U.S. open skies template signed with 10 other countries.
Such a move may trigger complaints from those countries, said Yohe.
The open skies talks were due to kick off on Tuesday but have been postponed for two weeks due to a senior UK official being taken ill.
